cheng: Heads-up: on prod-12 we observed steady RSS growth in the kv_store process tied to longctx chat sessions. Host-level RAM climbs over ~30 minutes during high-turn chat bursts and one tenant's KV residency keeps increasing, fragmenting pages. Anyone seen this pattern?

maya: Hmm, can you paste a heap/pprof snapshot? :eyes:

cheng: Pasted a trimmed heap topo from pprof: ```# net/http/pprof heap
  12.4MB  24.8MB  github.com/redwood/serving/kv.(*Shard).AllocPage
   9.1MB  18.2MB  github.com/redwood/serving/kv.(*SessionKV).Snapshot
   6.0MB   6.0MB  github.com/redwood/serving/kv.(*Page).MarkReferenced
  ...
Total allocated: 1.9GB, Inuse: 1.3GB, RSS: 2.1GB
Top by owner: tenant:t-123 -> 820MB resident pages, tenant:t-45 -> 140MB
```

loren: That looks like reuse rate is low for t-123 pages. Could be a longctx access pattern where the tenant appends long transcripts and we never hit the same KV keys again, so residency keeps growing. Are we leaking refs or just poor eviction aggressiveness?

sam: Two things to check: 1) batching heuristics that create many short-lived sessions may pin pages during in-flight requests; 2) kernel selection for the runtime can affect how we prefetch/prime KV pages into GPU staging — but this sounds mostly host-RAM side.

perf-bot: alert: kv-residency-anomaly detected on prod-12 at 03:12 UTC. Top offender: tenant t-123, residency growth +48% in 15m. Host: gpu-12a, shard: s7.

maya: Repro steps I'd try: run the longctx-burst-playback on staging with payloads that append 1k token messages at 2 req/s for 30m. Use `REPLAY_MODE=longctx_burst` and `--tenant t-123` so we match access locality. Example: ```./tools/replayer --mode longctx_burst --tenant t-123 --rate 2 --duration 1800```

cheng: I ran a shorter 10m run on staging. Observed same slope but lower amplitude. Also saw page fragmentation metric tick up: `kv.page_frag_ratio` went from 0.12 -> 0.38.

loren: For mitigation, we can do: a) introduce residency decay (exponential half-life) so old pages age out even if still referenced rarely; b) tighten soft per-tenant quotas (soft cap + burst tokens) so a tenant can't hoard 70% of page slots; c) trigger periodic compaction that coalesces partially used slabs.

sam: Agree. On (a) the residency score math currently is purely LRU-ish with sticky increments on access. Proposed quick change: residency = residency * exp(-dt/half_life) + access_boost, recompute on checkpoint. Half-life candidate: 10m. That should make long-tail pages decay without heavy eviction churn.

maya: Short-term ops play: set soft quota for tenants at 25% of shard pages, allow burst to 40% for 2m, then force background eviction. We should notify AE teams if we throttle.

perf-bot: note: added timeline alert rule `kv.residency.surge` to staging with threshold 30% sustained for 10m.

cheng: Action items: 1) I'll open an RFC for residency-decay + half-life math and run bench sims (cheng/RFC-#347). 2) @maya please run the longctx-burst-replayer in staging with current soft-quota tweak. 3) @loren please prototype a compaction job that runs during low-load windows. 4) @sam add per-tenant 'paged_eviction_stall' metric and a page-reuse-latency histogram.

loren: I'll prototype compactor: plan is to scan slabs with frag_ratio > 0.25 and try to migrate hot pages into contiguous runs, then free whole slabs. Might need transient locking; will benchmark.

maya: Running reproducer now on staging (started 03:40 UTC). Will paste pprof + `kv.page_frag_ratio` after 20m. :thumbsup:

sam: Also add a small test in the runtime perf harness to simulate multi-tenant noisy neighbor: spin up 10 tenants with skewed longctx patterns and measure max residency skew. Want a regression test before we change defaults.

cheng: Good. Let's aim to have a short sync tomorrow 10:30am PT to review RFC and staging numbers. I'll link RFC in this thread when opened. Thanks all. :rocket:
